claim: The retromer complex directly and specifically regulates Notch receptor retrograde trafficking in Drosophila neuroblast lineages to ensure unidirectional Notch signaling from neural progenitors to neuroblasts.
source: Here we show that the retromer complex directly and specifically regulates Notch receptor retrograde trafficking in Drosophila neuroblast lineages to ensure the unidirectional Notch signaling from neural progenitors to neuroblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including colocalization studies, coimmunoprecipitation experiments, and genetic rescue experiments.

claim: Notch polyubiquitination mediated by E3 ubiquitin ligase Itch/Su(dx) is inherently inefficient within neural progenitors.
source: Notch polyubiquitination mediated by E3 ubiquitin ligase Itch/Su(dx) is inherently inefficient within neural progenitors, relying on retromer-mediated trafficking to avoid aberrant endosomal accumulation of Notch and cell-autonomous signaling activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing synergistic genetic interactions between Su(dx) and Vps26, and by the observation that Su(dx) and Ndfip have distinct subcellular localizations.

claim: Upon retromer dysfunction, hypo-ubiquitinated Notch accumulates in Rab7+ enlarged endosomes.
source: Upon retromer dysfunction, hypo-ubiquitinated Notch accumulates in Rab7+ enlarged endosomes, where it is ectopically processed and activated in a ligand-dependent manner, causing progenitor-originated tumorigenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing Notch accumulation in enlarged Rab7+ endosomes in vps35 mutants, and Western blot data showing accumulation of hypo-ubiquitinated NICD fragments.

claim: Ectopic Notch activation in vps35 mutants occurs in a ligand-dependent manner.
source: Upon retromer dysfunction, hypo-ubiquitinated Notch accumulates in Rab7+ enlarged endosomes, where it is ectopically processed and activated in a ligand-dependent manner, causing progenitor-originated tumorigenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic experiments showing that expression of dominant negative Delta or Kuzbanian suppresses the vps35 mutant phenotype.

claim: Retromer dysfunction causes progenitor-originated tumorigenesis.
source: Upon retromer dysfunction, hypo-ubiquitinated Notch accumulates in Rab7+ enlarged endosomes, where it is ectopically processed and activated in a ligand-dependent manner, causing progenitor-originated tumorigenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by transplantation assays showing that vps35 mutant brain tissue forms tumors and metastasizes in host flies.

claim: The correct establishment and maintenance of unidirectional Notch signaling are critical for the homeostasis of various stem cell lineages.
source: The correct establishment and maintenance of unidirectional Notch signaling are critical for the homeostasis of various stem cell lineages (Bertet et al., 2014; Blanpain et al., 2006; Bowman et al., 2008; Conboy and Rando, 2002; Fre et al., 2005; Guo and Ohlstein, 2015; Lin et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2017; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Ren et al., 2018; Song and Lu, 2011; Williams et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Canonical Notch signaling requires two adjacent cells to present transmembrane ligands and transmembrane receptors respectively.
source: The canonical Notch signaling, which requires two adjacent cells to present transmembrane ligands and transmembrane receptors respectively (Bray, 2006; Kopan and Ilagan, 2009) and involves intercellular or intracellular amplification step(s) to establish its unidirectionality (Artavanis-Tsakonas et al., 1999; Liu et al., 2017; Losick and Desplan, 2008), is an ideal signaling pathway for binary cell fate specification.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature on Notch signaling.

claim: Notch signaling has been implicated in cell fate decision-making events in diverse stem cell lineages.
source: Accordingly, Notch signaling has been implicated in cell fate decision-making events in diverse stem cell lineages (Bertet et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2016; Demitrack et al., 2015; Dong et al., 2012; Hilton et al., 2008; Homem and Knoblich, 2012; Liu et al., 2010; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Pinto-Teixeira et al., 2018; Watt et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Asymmetric segregation of the endocytic protein Numb is an important strategy utilized by dividing stem cells or progenitors to ensure binary cell fate decisions.
source: An important strategy utilized by dividing stem cells or progenitors to ensure binary cell fate decisions is asymmetric segregation of the endocytic protein Numb, an evolutionarily conserved Notch signaling antagonist, to one of the daughter cells (Bultje et al., 2009; Conboy and Rando, 2002; Gunage et al., 2014; Lu et al., 1998; Luo et al., 2005; Rhyu et al., 1994; Sallé et al., 2017; Shen et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2017; Zhong et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Numb is an evolutionarily conserved Notch signaling antagonist.
source: An important strategy utilized by dividing stem cells or progenitors to ensure binary cell fate decisions is asymmetric segregation of the endocytic protein Numb, an evolutionarily conserved Notch signaling antagonist, to one of the daughter cells (Bultje et al., 2009; Conboy and Rando, 2002; Gunage et al., 2014; Lu et al., 1998; Luo et al., 2005; Rhyu et al., 1994; Sallé et al., 2017; Shen et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2017; Zhong et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Numb acts as an adaptor to bridge the Notch receptor and its cofactor(s) with the endocytic machinery and reduces the surface pool of Notch by promoting its endocytosis.
source: Numb acts as an adaptor to bridge the Notch receptor and its cofactor(s) with the endocytic machinery and reduces the surface pool of Notch by promoting its endocytosis (Hutterer and Knoblich, 2005; Song and Lu, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Endocytosed Notch receptors are often poly-ubiquitinated by E3 ubiquitin ligases, such as Itch/Su(dx) and Nedd4.
source: Endocytosed Notch receptors are often poly-ubiquitinated by E3 ubiquitin ligases, such as Itch/Su(dx) (Suppressor of deltex) and Nedd4 (Cornell et al., 1999; Le Bras et al., 2011; Qiu et al., 2000; Sakata et al., 2004; Wilkin et al., 2004), and sorted through the ESCRT (Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport) pathway for lysosomal degradation (Horner et al., 2018; Thompson et al., 2005; Vaccari et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Poly-ubiquitinated Notch receptors are sorted through the ESCRT pathway for lysosomal degradation.
source: Endocytosed Notch receptors are often poly-ubiquitinated by E3 ubiquitin ligases, such as Itch/Su(dx) (Suppressor of deltex) and Nedd4 (Cornell et al., 1999; Le Bras et al., 2011; Qiu et al., 2000; Sakata et al., 2004; Wilkin et al., 2004), and sorted through the ESCRT (Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport) pathway for lysosomal degradation (Horner et al., 2018; Thompson et al., 2005; Vaccari et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The daughter cell inheriting relatively more Numb protein becomes the Notch signaling sending cell.
source: As a consequence, the daughter cell inheriting relatively more Numb protein becomes the Notch signaling sending cell, unambiguously establishing signaling directionality.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the established role of Numb in Notch signaling.

claim: Dysregulation in the asymmetric segregation of Numb has been implicated in a wide range of developmental defects and diseases.
source: Not surprisingly, dysregulation in the asymmetric segregation of Numb has been implicated in a wide range of developmental defects and diseases (Bowman et al., 2008; Bu et al., 2016; Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005; George et al., 2013; Li et al., 2003; Pece et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The proteolytic activity of γ-secretase has been detected in endosomal membranes.
source: The proteolytic activity of γ-secretase has been detected in endosomal membranes (Gupta-Rossi et al., 2004; Lah and Levey, 2000; Pasternak et al., 2003; Urra et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The relatively low pH at the endosomal compartments renders a conformational change in the Notch receptor, allowing for more efficient proteolysis.
source: Furthermore, it has been postulated that the relatively low pH at the endosomal compartments renders a conformational change in the Notch receptor, allowing for more efficient proteolysis.
evidence: The claim is presented as a postulation based on previous work.

claim: Inactivation of the ESCRT complex leads to retention of the Notch receptor in the limiting membrane of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) where Notch is ectopically activated via ligand-independent, γ-secretase-dependent proteolysis.
source: Indeed, inactivation of the ESCRT complex leads to retention of the Notch receptor in the limiting membrane of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) where Notch is ectopically activated via ligand-independent, γ-secretase-dependent proteolysis (Hori et al., 2011; Thompson et al., 2005; Vaccari and Bilder, 2005; Vaccari et al., 2009; Wilkin et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Type II neural stem cells in the Drosophila larval central brain region provide an attractive model system for studying how endosomal trafficking establishes unidirectional Notch signaling.
source: Type II neural stem cells, so called neuroblasts, in the Drosophila larval central brain region provide an attractive model system for studying how endosomal trafficking establishes unidirectional Notch signaling and ensures stem cell versus progenitor binary cell fate decisions (Figure 1A) (Liu et al., 2017; Song and Lu, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and by the rationale provided in the manuscript.

claim: Type II neural stem cell lineages resemble their mammalian counterparts in terms of regulatory molecules and principles, yet with much simpler anatomical structure and lineage composition.
source: Firstly, type II neural stem cell lineages resemble their mammalian counterparts in terms of regulatory molecules and principles, yet with much simpler anatomical structure and lineage composition (Brand and Livesey, 2011; Homem and Knoblich, 2012; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Unidirectional Notch signaling is critical for establishing type II neuroblast versus immature intermediate neural progenitor (INP) binary cell fates.
source: Secondly, unidirectional Notch signaling is critical for establishing type II neuroblast versus immature intermediate neural progenitor (INP) binary cell fates (Bowman et al., 2008; Song and Lu, 2011; Song and Lu, 2012; Wang et al., 2006; Weng et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Downregulation of Notch signaling in neuroblasts leads to their premature differentiation into INPs and loss of stemness.
source: Whereas downregulation of Notch signaling in neuroblasts leads to their premature differentiation into INPs and loss of stemness, overactivation of Notch signaling in neural progenitors cause their fate reversion back into neuroblast-like state and tumorigenesis (Bowman et al., 2008; Song and Lu, 2011; Song and Lu, 2012; Wang et al., 2006; Weng et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Overactivation of Notch signaling in neural progenitors causes their fate reversion back into neuroblast-like state and tumorigenesis.
source: Whereas downregulation of Notch signaling in neuroblasts leads to their premature differentiation into INPs and loss of stemness, overactivation of Notch signaling in neural progenitors cause their fate reversion back into neuroblast-like state and tumorigenesis (Bowman et al., 2008; Song and Lu, 2011; Song and Lu, 2012; Wang et al., 2006; Weng et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The total number of neuroblasts in each brain lobe represents a quantitative and precise readout of Notch signaling strength.
source: Thus, the total number of neuroblasts in each brain lobe represents a quantitative and precise readout of Notch signaling strength.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the established role of Notch signaling in neuroblast maintenance.

claim: Numb is asymmetrically inherited by immature INPs, where it dampens Notch signaling partly by reducing the cell surface pool of mature Notch receptors.
source: Thirdly, Numb is asymmetrically inherited by immature INPs, where it dampens Notch signaling partly by reducing the cell surface pool of mature Notch receptors (Figure 1B) (Bowman et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2006b; Song and Lu, 2012; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Vps26 was identified in a large-scale unbiased RNAi-based genetic screen for regulators of neuroblast versus progenitor cell fate decision.
source: In a large-scale unbiased RNAi-based genetic screen for regulators of neuroblast versus progenitor cell fate decision, we identified Vps26, a subunit of the retromer complex (Burd and Cullen, 2014; Wang and Bellen, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the experimental approach.

claim: Specific downregulation of Vps26 in Drosophila central brain neuroblast lineages led to a supernumerous neuroblast phenotype.
source: Specific downregulation of Vps26 in Drosophila central brain neuroblast lineages led to a supernumerous neuroblast phenotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The retromer complex is an evolutionarily highly conserved endosomal sorting complex.
source: The retromer complex is an evolutionarily highly conserved endosomal sorting complex, which plays a crucial role in the retrograde trafficking of a specific subset of endocytosed proteins from endosomes back to the trans-Golgi network or the plasma membrane (Burd and Cullen, 2014; Wang and Bellen, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The retromer complex plays a crucial role in the retrograde trafficking of a specific subset of endocytosed proteins from endosomes back to the trans-Golgi network or the plasma membrane.
source: The retromer complex is an evolutionarily highly conserved endosomal sorting complex, which plays a crucial role in the retrograde trafficking of a specific subset of endocytosed proteins from endosomes back to the trans-Golgi network or the plasma membrane (Burd and Cullen, 2014; Wang and Bellen, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The core of the retromer complex is a vacuolar protein sorting (Vps) trimer composed of Vps35, Vps26 and Vps29 subunits.
source: The core of the retromer complex is a vacuolar protein sorting (Vps) trimer composed of Vps35, Vps26 and Vps29 subunits (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about retromer structure and is illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Retromer has been implicated in controlling a wide range of physiological processes, such as regulating fly wing development, maintaining the function of photoreceptors, establishing cell polarity in epithelial cells, controlling LTP in mature hippocampus, modulating fly oogenesis and propagating mitochondrial stress signals.
source: Previous studies have implicated retromer in controlling a wide range of physiological processes, such as regulating fly wing development, maintaining the function of photoreceptors, establishing cell polarity in epithelial cells, controlling LTP (long-term potential) in mature hippocampus, modulating fly oogenesis and propagating mitochondrial stress signals (Belenkaya et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2010; Choy et al., 2014; Coudreuse et al., 2006; Franch-Marro et al., 2008; Gomez-Lamarca et al., 2015; Harterink et al., 2011; Hesketh et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2008; Pocha et al., 2011; Port et al., 2008; Starble and Pokrywka, 2018; Temkin et al., 2011; Temkin et al., 2017; Wang and Bellen, 2015; Yang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Dysfunction of retromer-mediated endosomal sorting has been linked to various pathologies, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease.
source: Dysfunction of retromer-mediated endosomal sorting has been linked to various pathologies, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease (McMillan et al., 2017; Small and Petsko, 2015; Wang and Bellen, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The brain tumor phenotype induced by vps26-RNAi was fully rescued by the coexpression of a shmiRNA-resistant form of the Vps26 transgene.
source: Such brain tumor phenotype induced by vps26-RNAi was fully rescued by the coexpression of a shmiRNA-resistant form of the Vps26 transgene, excluding the possibility of an off-target effect of the shmiRNA (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Homozygous vps35 mutant larval brains exhibited an even more severe supernumerary neuroblast phenotype than vps26-IR.
source: Furthermore, homozygous vps35 mutant larval brains exhibited an even more severe supernumerary neuroblast phenotype than vps26-IR, and such phenotype was fully rescued upon specific expression of a Vps35 transgene in all central brain neuroblast lineages (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The vps35 mutant phenotype was fully rescued upon specific expression of a Vps35 transgene in all central brain neuroblast lineages.
source: Furthermore, homozygous vps35 mutant larval brains exhibited an even more severe supernumerary neuroblast phenotype than vps26-IR, and such phenotype was fully rescued upon specific expression of a Vps35 transgene in all central brain neuroblast lineages (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Human Vps35 fully rescued the brain tumor phenotype of vps35 mutants back to wild type.
source: Importantly, human Vps35 also fully rescued the brain tumor phenotype of vps35 mutants back to wild type (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Retromer plays an evolutionarily-conserved role in preventing ectopic neuroblast formation in the central brain area.
source: Taken together, our results clearly indicated that retromer plays an evolutionarily-conserved role in preventing ectopic neuroblast formation in the central brain area.
evidence: The claim is based on the rescue experiments with human Vps35.

claim: Expression of the Vps35 transgene in type II neuroblast lineages, by PntP1-Gal4, fully suppressed the brain tumor phenotype caused by vps35 mutation.
source: Expression of the Vps35 transgene in type II neuroblast lineages, by PntP1-Gal4 (Zhu et al., 2011), fully suppressed the brain tumor phenotype caused by vps35 mutation (Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: Restoring Vps35 function in type I neuroblast lineages, by ase-Gal4, failed to suppress the vps35 mutant phenotype.
source: By contrast, restoring Vps35 function in type I neuroblast lineages, by ase-Gal4 (Zhu et al., 2006), failed to do so (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: The ectopic neuroblasts in retromer mutants are derived from type II neuroblast lineages.
source: These results indicated that the ectopic neuroblasts in retromer mutants are derived from type II neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is based on the lineage-specific rescue experiments.

claim: Expression of the Vps35 transgene in Dpn- Ase- INPs by erm-Gal4 (II) but not in Dpn- Ase+ INPs by erm-Gal4 (III) completely rescued the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype caused by Vps35 inactivation.
source: Indeed, expression of the Vps35 transgene in Deadpan (Dpn)- Asense (Ase)- INPs by erm-Gal4 (II) but not in Dpn- Ase+ INPs by erm-Gal4 (III) (Pfeiffer et al., 2008) completely rescued the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype caused by Vps35 inactivation (Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: The reverting Dpn-Ase- neural progenitors are the cellular origin of brain tumor in vps35 mutants.
source: Therefore, the reverting Dpn-Ase- neural progenitors are the cellular origin of brain tumor in vps35 mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on the lineage-specific rescue experiments.

claim: Cell polarity remained unaltered in vps35 mutant neuroblasts.
source: Supporting this notion, cell polarity remained unaltered in vps35 mutant neuroblasts (Figure 1G), indicating that these ectopic neuroblasts are not resulted from neuroblast symmetric division.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Numb is normally localized to the basal cortex of vps35 mutant dividing neuroblasts.
source: Importantly, Numb is normally localized to the basal cortex of vps35 mutant dividing neuroblasts (Figure 1H), arguing against the possibility that defective asymmetric segregation of Numb causes INP dedifferentiation in vps35 mutant brains.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Vps26 downregulation in type II neuroblast lineages or immature INP lineages resulted in supernumerary neuroblast phenotype.
source: Consistently, whereas Vps26 downregulation in type II neuroblast lineages or immature INP lineages, driven by PntP1-Gal4 or erm-Gal4(II) respectively, resulted in supernumerary neuroblast phenotype, its knockdown in mature INP lineages or type I neuroblast lineages, driven by erm-Gal4 (III) or ase-Gal4 respectively, failed to induce ectopic neuroblasts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vps26 knockdown in mature INP lineages or type I neuroblast lineages failed to induce ectopic neuroblasts.
source: Consistently, whereas Vps26 downregulation in type II neuroblast lineages or immature INP lineages, driven by PntP1-Gal4 or erm-Gal4(II) respectively, resulted in supernumerary neuroblast phenotype, its knockdown in mature INP lineages or type I neuroblast lineages, driven by erm-Gal4 (III) or ase-Gal4 respectively, failed to induce ectopic neuroblasts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Wild type control type II neuroblast MARCM clones contained one and only one Dpn+ Ase- neuroblast.
source: Furthermore, distinct from wild type control type II neuroblast MARCM clones (Lee and Luo, 1999) that contained one and only one Dpn+ Ase- neuroblast (white bracket in Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), vps35 mutant clones contained multiple ectopic Dpn+ Ase- Pros- neuroblast-like cells (yellow arrowheads in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3) several cell diameters away from the primary neuroblast (white bracket in Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: vps35 mutant clones contained multiple ectopic Dpn+ Ase- Pros- neuroblast-like cells several cell diameters away from the primary neuroblast.
source: Furthermore, distinct from wild type control type II neuroblast MARCM clones (Lee and Luo, 1999) that contained one and only one Dpn+ Ase- neuroblast (white bracket in Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), vps35 mutant clones contained multiple ectopic Dpn+ Ase- Pros- neuroblast-like cells (yellow arrowheads in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3) several cell diameters away from the primary neuroblast (white bracket in Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The ectopic Dpn+ Ase- Pros- neuroblast-like cells in vps35 mutants were of intermediate cell sizes between neural progenitors and primary neuroblasts, indicating that they were undergoing dedifferentiation.
source: These ectopic Dpn+ Ase- Pros- neuroblast-like cells were of intermediate cell sizes between neural progenitors and primary neuroblasts (yellow arrowheads in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3), indicating that they were undergoing dedifferentiation (Song and Lu, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I and inference based on cell size.

claim: FLP-FRT-based lineage tracing by inducing GFP+ clones exclusively in immature INPs resulted in labeling of INPs, GMCs, and neurons in wild-type brains.
source: In addition, FLP-FRT-based lineage tracing by inducing GFP+ clones exclusively in immature INPs, driven by erm-Gal4 (II), resulted in labeling of INPs (white arrowhead in Figure 1—figure supplement 4), GMCs, and neurons (cyan arrowhead in Figure 1—figure supplement 4) in wild-type brains.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: In vps35 mutant brains, GFP-labeled ectopic type II neuroblasts of various cellular sizes were found after lineage tracing.
source: In contrast, in vps35 mutant brains, GFP-labeled ectopic type II neuroblasts of various cellular sizes were found after similar lineage tracing (yellow arrowheads in Figure 1—figure supplement 4), indicating that immature INPs could indeed dedifferentiate back into neuroblast-like cells upon retromer dysfunction.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Immature INPs could dedifferentiate back into neuroblast-like cells upon retromer dysfunction.
source: In contrast, in vps35 mutant brains, GFP-labeled ectopic type II neuroblasts of various cellular sizes were found after similar lineage tracing (yellow arrowheads in Figure 1—figure supplement 4), indicating that immature INPs could indeed dedifferentiate back into neuroblast-like cells upon retromer dysfunction.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The brain tumor phenotype in vps35 mutants is caused by cell fate reversion of Dpn- Ase- neural progenitors.
source: Taken together, our results clearly indicate that the brain tumor phenotype in vps35 mutants is caused by cell fate reversion of Dpn- Ase- neural progenitors.
evidence: The claim is based on multiple lines of experimental evidence including lineage tracing and MARCM analysis.

claim: Transplantation of vps35 mutant but not wild-type control brain tissues into the abdomens of host flies caused the formation of massive tumors.
source: Transplantation of vps35 mutant but not wild-type control brain tissues into the abdomens of host flies caused the formation of massive tumors (yellow bracket in Figure 1J) that often metastasize to distal organs (yellow arrowhead in Figure 1J; statistic results in Figure 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J,K.

claim: vps35 mutant tumors often metastasize to distal organs.
source: Transplantation of vps35 mutant but not wild-type control brain tissues into the abdomens of host flies caused the formation of massive tumors (yellow bracket in Figure 1J) that often metastasize to distal organs (yellow arrowhead in Figure 1J; statistic results in Figure 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J,K.

claim: The vps35 mutant GFP+ tumor cells extracted from the abdomen of transplanted hosts were Dpn+ Miranda (Mira)+ neuroblast-like cells.
source: Importantly, the vps35 mutant GFP+ tumor cells extracted from the abdomen of transplanted hosts were Dpn+ Miranda (Mira)+ neuroblast-like cells (Figure 1L).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: vps35 mutant cells in the larval brains are tumor-initiating cells.
source: Thus vps35 mutant cells in the larval brains are indeed tumor-initiating cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the transplantation assay results.

claim: Retromer acts as a tumor suppressor in the Drosophila brain by preventing neural progenitor dedifferentiation.
source: Together, we conclude that retromer acts as a tumor suppressor in the Drosophila brain by preventing neural progenitor dedifferentiation.
evidence: The claim is based on the combined results of genetic and transplantation experiments.

claim: vps35 mutant INPs or ectopic neuroblasts displayed dramatically enlarged late endosomes/MVBs compared to wild-type control INPs.
source: Compared to wild-type control INPs, vps35 mutant INPs or ectopic neuroblasts displayed dramatically enlarged late endosomes/MVBs (Figure 2A–C; up to more than 10-fold increase in endosomal vesicle sizes).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The expression levels of Rab7 remained unchanged in vps35 mutants.
source: The expression levels of Rab7 remained unchanged in vps35 mutants (Figure 2D), ruling out the likelihood that Vps35 regulates Rab7 gene expression or protein stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Rab7 primarily colocalized with early endosome marker Rab5 in vps35 but not wild type cells.
source: Furthermore, Rab7 primarily colocalized with early endosome marker Rab5 in vps35 but not wild type cells (Figure 2E), demonstrating that the enlarged MVBs in vps35 mutant cells are of early and late endosome hybrid identities.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The enlarged MVBs in vps35 mutant cells are of early and late endosome hybrid identities.
source: Furthermore, Rab7 primarily colocalized with early endosome marker Rab5 in vps35 but not wild type cells (Figure 2E), demonstrating that the enlarged MVBs in vps35 mutant cells are of early and late endosome hybrid identities.
evidence: The claim is based on the colocalization data of Rab7 and Rab5.

claim: Other subcellular markers including lysosome (GFP-LAMP1), recycling endosome (Rab11), Golgi (GFP-Golgi) and mitochondria (mito-GFP) remained unchanged in vps35-defective cells.
source: In contrast, other subcellular markers including lysosome (GFP-LAMP1), recycling endosome (Rab11), Golgi (GFP-Golgi) and mitochondria (mito-GFP) remained unchanged in vps35-defective cells (Figure 2F–2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F-I.

claim: Retromer normally functions in neural progenitors to transport cargo proteins away from early and late endosomes.
source: Therefore, our results strongly suggest that retromer normally functions in neural progenitors to transport cargo proteins away from early and late endosomes.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation of enlarged endosomes in vps35 mutants.

claim: Upon retromer dysfunction, its cargo proteins highly accumulate in MVBs, resulting in enlarged, aberrant endosomal vesicles of hybrid identities.
source: Upon retromer dysfunction, its cargo proteins highly accumulate in MVBs, resulting in enlarged, aberrant endosomal vesicles of hybrid identities.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation of enlarged endosomes with hybrid identities in vps35 mutants.

claim: The Notch receptor and its cofactor Sanpodo highly accumulated in enlarged puncta in vps35 mutant cells, mostly colocalizing with Rab7+ enlarged endosomes.
source: We noted that the Notch receptor and its cofactor Sanpodo (Couturier et al., 2012; Hutterer and Knoblich, 2005; O'Connor-Giles and Skeath, 2003; Song and Lu, 2012) highly accumulated in enlarged puncta in vps35 mutant cells, mostly colocalizing with Rab7+ enlarged endosomes (Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The distribution of other signaling molecules such as Patched (Ptc) and Wnt/Wingless (Wg) remained unaltered upon Vps35 depletion.
source: In contrast, the distribution of other signaling molecules such as Patched (Ptc) and Wnt/Wingless (Wg) remained unaltered upon Vps35 depletion (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C), indicating that retromer specifically mediates Notch receptor trafficking in neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Retromer specifically mediates Notch receptor trafficking in neuroblast lineages.
source: In contrast, the distribution of other signaling molecules such as Patched (Ptc) and Wnt/Wingless (Wg) remained unaltered upon Vps35 depletion (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C), indicating that retromer specifically mediates Notch receptor trafficking in neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is based on the selective accumulation of Notch but not other signaling molecules in vps35 mutants.

claim: Notch signaling reporter E(spl)mγ-GFP was undetectable in wild type Dpn- Ase- immature INPs but ectopically turned on in Dpn+ Ase- dedifferentiating neural progenitors upon Vps26 downregulation.
source: Strongly supporting this notion, Notch signaling reporter E(spl)mγ-GFP (Almeida and Bray, 2005; Song and Lu, 2011), which faithfully reflects Notch signaling activity in neuroblast lineages, was undetectable in wild type Dpn- Ase- immature INPs (white arrowhead in Figure 3C) but ectopically turned on in Dpn+ Ase- dedifferentiating neural progenitors (yellow arrowhead in Figure 3C) upon Vps26 downregulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Notch puncta colocalizing with Rab7+ endosomes remained unaltered in vps35 mutant wing imaginal disc epithelia.
source: In addition, Notch puncta colocalizing with Rab7+ endosomes remained unaltered in vps35 mutant wing imaginal disc epithelia (arrowheads in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D), suggesting a tissue-specific regulation of Notch trafficking by retromer.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Retromer regulates Notch trafficking in a tissue-specific manner.
source: In addition, Notch puncta colocalizing with Rab7+ endosomes remained unaltered in vps35 mutant wing imaginal disc epithelia (arrowheads in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D), suggesting a tissue-specific regulation of Notch trafficking by retromer.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation that Notch trafficking is affected in neuroblasts but not in wing disc epithelia.

claim: Retromer normally suppresses Notch activity through mediating retrograde trafficking of Notch receptors in neural progenitors.
source: Collectively, retromer normally suppresses Notch activity through mediating retrograde trafficking of Notch receptors in neural progenitors.
evidence: The claim is based on the combined observations of Notch accumulation and ectopic activation in vps35 mutants.

claim: Neuroblast lineage-specific knockdown of Notch completely suppressed the neuroblast overproliferation phenotype in vps35 mutants.
source: Neuroblast lineage-specific knockdown of Notch completely suppressed the neuroblast overproliferation phenotype in vps35 mutants (Figure 3D,E), indicating that the dedifferentiation process of vps35 mutant INPs was Notch signaling-dependent.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: The dedifferentiation process of vps35 mutant INPs was Notch signaling-dependent.
source: Neuroblast lineage-specific knockdown of Notch completely suppressed the neuroblast overproliferation phenotype in vps35 mutants (Figure 3D,E), indicating that the dedifferentiation process of vps35 mutant INPs was Notch signaling-dependent.
evidence: The claim is based on the genetic rescue experiment with Notch-RNAi.

claim: Type II neuroblast lineage-specific or immature INP-specific depletion of the ligand Delta completely or potently suppressed brain tumor phenotypes caused by vps35 mutations.
source: Type II neuroblast lineage-specific or immature INP-specific depletion of the ligand Delta, as well as neuroblast lineage-specific expression of a dominant negative form of Delta (Dl-DN) that lacks its intracellular domain (Baonza et al., 2000; Flores et al., 2000; Huppert et al., 1997), completely or potently suppressed brain tumor phenotypes caused by vps35 mutations (Figure 3D,E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Type II neuroblast lineage-specific or immature INP-specific expression of a dominant negative form of the metalloprotease Kuzbanian (Kuz-DN) phenocopied the effect of Notch-RNAi in inhibiting brain tumor formation.
source: Furthermore, type II neuroblast lineage-specific or immature INP-specific expression of a dominant negative form of the metalloprotease Kuzbanian (Kuz-DN), which lacks its protease activity and thereby specifically blocks ligand-induce S2 cleavage of Notch (Lieber et al., 2002; Mumm et al., 2000; Pan and Rubin, 1997), also phenocopied the effect of Notch-RNAi in inhibiting brain tumor formation (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Overactivation of Notch signaling in vps35 mutant neural progenitors is largely, if not completely, ligand-dependent.
source: These observations indicated that overactivation of Notch signaling in vps35 mutant neural progenitors is largely, if not completely, ligand-dependent.
evidence: The claim is based on the genetic rescue experiments with Delta and Kuzbanian.

claim: A functional γ–secretase is essential for ectopic activation of Notch signaling in vps35 mutants.
source: Not surprisingly, a functional γ–secretase is also essential for ectopic activation of Notch signaling in vps35 mutants (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Inactivation of various other signaling pathways, such as Wnt/Wg, Hedgehog or EGFR, or overactivation of Hedgehog signaling showed no effects on the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutants.
source: In sharp contrast, inactivation of various other signaling pathways, such as Wnt/Wg, Hedgehog or EGFR, or overactivation of Hedgehog signaling showed no effects on the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutants (Figure 3D,E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F), further demonstrating the high specificity of retromer on Notch signaling pathway in neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Notch colocalized with fly or human Vps35 transgene and endogenous Vps26.
source: Importantly, Notch colocalized with fly or human Vps35 transgene (Figure 3F,G) and endogenous Vps26 (Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F,G,H.

claim: Notch depletion by RNAi led to a dramatic reduction in Rab7+ endosomal vesicle sizes almost back to normal.
source: More remarkably, Notch depletion by RNAi led to a dramatic reduction in Rab7+ endosomal vesicle sizes almost back to normal (Figure 3I), suggesting that Notch receptors constitute the major endosomal contents of these aberrant vps35 mutant vesicles.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Notch receptors constitute the major endosomal contents of the aberrant vps35 mutant vesicles.
source: More remarkably, Notch depletion by RNAi led to a dramatic reduction in Rab7+ endosomal vesicle sizes almost back to normal (Figure 3I), suggesting that Notch receptors constitute the major endosomal contents of these aberrant vps35 mutant vesicles.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation that Notch depletion reduces endosomal size.

claim: The Notch receptor is a functionally important cargo of retromer in type II neuroblast lineages.
source: Taken together, our results strongly suggested that the Notch receptor is a functionally important cargo of retromer in type II neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is based on multiple lines of evidence including colocalization, genetic interactions, and rescue experiments.

claim: Vps35 or Vps26 was specifically coimmunoprecipitated with Notch intracellular domain (NICD) from HEK293T cell extracts.
source: Vps35 or Vps26 was specifically coimmunoprecipitated with Notch intracellular domain (NICD) from HEK293T cell extracts (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The ankyrin repeat region but not the C-terminal region of NICD exhibited a strong binding activity to Vps26.
source: Further domain mapping experiments revealed that the ankyrin repeat region but not the C-terminal region of NICD exhibited a strong binding activity to Vps26 (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Vps26 utilized its middle domain to interact with NICD.
source: Reciprocal coIP assay showed that Vps26 utilized its middle domain to interact with NICD (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: Notch-V5 expressed in central brain neuroblast lineages was specifically coimmunoprecipitated with Vps35-FLAG from fly larval brain extracts.
source: Furthermore, Notch-V5 expressed in central brain neuroblast lineages was specifically coimmunoprecipitated with Vps35-FLAG from fly larval brain extracts (Figure 4F), confirming the in vivo protein-protein interaction.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Mouse NICD and mouse Vps26 proteins physically interact.
source: Importantly, coIP experiments further revealed interaction between mouse NICD and mouse Vps26 proteins (Figure 4G,H), indicating that the physical association between the retromer cargo-recognition complex and Notch is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: The physical association between the retromer cargo-recognition complex and Notch is evolutionarily conserved.
source: Importantly, coIP experiments further revealed interaction between mouse NICD and mouse Vps26 proteins (Figure 4G,H), indicating that the physical association between the retromer cargo-recognition complex and Notch is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation of physical interaction in both fly and mouse systems.

claim: The Notch receptor is a bona fide cargo protein of the retromer complex.
source: Taken together, our results validate that the Notch receptor is a bona fide cargo protein of the retromer complex.
evidence: The claim is based on the coimmunoprecipitation experiments demonstrating physical interaction.

claim: Overexpression of a dominant negative form of Rab5 GTPase (Rab5-DN) completely suppressed brain tumor formation in vps35 mutant brains.
source: Indeed, overexpression of a dominant negative form of Rab5 GTPase (Rab5-DN), which blocks the fusion of endocytic vesicles with early endosomes, or a constitutively active form of Rab9 GTPase (Rab9-CA), which promotes protein retrograde trafficking from late endosomes to trans-Golgi network (TGN) or the plasma membrane (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), completely suppressed brain tumor formation in vps35 mutant brains (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Overexpression of a constitutively active form of Rab9 GTPase (Rab9-CA) completely suppressed brain tumor formation in vps35 mutant brains.
source: Indeed, overexpression of a dominant negative form of Rab5 GTPase (Rab5-DN), which blocks the fusion of endocytic vesicles with early endosomes, or a constitutively active form of Rab9 GTPase (Rab9-CA), which promotes protein retrograde trafficking from late endosomes to trans-Golgi network (TGN) or the plasma membrane (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), completely suppressed brain tumor formation in vps35 mutant brains (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Both the enlargement of Rab5/Rab7-positive endosomal vesicles and the high accumulation of Notch in these aberrant endosomal compartments in vps35 mutant cells were effectively relieved upon Rab5-DN or Rab9-CA coexpression.
source: Importantly, both the enlargement of Rab5/Rab7-positive endosomal vesicles and the high accumulation of Notch in these aberrant endosomal compartments in vps35 mutant cells were effectively relieved upon Rab5-DN or Rab9-CA coexpression (arrowheads in Figure 5D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Overexpression of a constitutively active form of Rab7 (Rab7-CA) or the ESCRT-0 complex component Hrs potently inhibited the neuroblast overproliferation phenotype in vps35 mutant brains.
source: On the other hand, overexpression of a constitutively active form of Rab7 (Rab7-CA) or the ESCRT-0 complex component Hrs (Hepatocyte growth factor-regulated tyrosine kinase substrate), which accelerates the protein trafficking towards lysosome (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) (Lloyd et al., 2002), potently inhibited the neuroblast overproliferation phenotype in vps35 mutant brains (Figure 5A,B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Coexpression of either Rab7-CA or Hrs led to high accumulation of Notch in lysosomes of vps35 mutant cells.
source: Indeed, coexpression of either Rab7-CA or Hrs led to high accumulation of Notch in lysosomes of vps35 mutant cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Overexpression of a constitutively active form of Rab5 GTPase (Rab5-CA), or a dominant negative form of Rab7 (Rab7-DN) or Rab9 (Rab9-DN) GTPase, failed to suppress the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutant brains.
source: In contrast, overexpression of a constitutively active form of Rab5 GTPase (Rab5-CA), which accelerates the fusion of endocytic vesicles with early endosomes, or a dominant negative form of Rab7 (Rab7-DN) or Rab9 (Rab9-DN) GTPase, which prevents transport of proteins away from the sorting endosomes, failed to suppress the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutant brains (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Delta ligand clearly colocalized with Rab7+ enlarged endosomes in vps35 mutant cells.
source: In addition, the Delta ligand clearly colocalized with Rab7+ enlarged endosomes in vps35 mutant cells (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The enlarged, aberrant endosomal vesicles with both early and late endosomal identities are the ligand-dependent activating compartments of the Notch receptor in vps35 mutant neural progenitors.
source: Taken together, we concluded that the enlarged, aberrant endosomal vesicles with both early and late endosomal identities are the ligand-dependent activating compartments of the Notch receptor in vps35 mutant neural progenitors.
evidence: The claim is based on multiple lines of evidence including colocalization of Notch and Delta, and genetic rescue experiments.

claim: Neuroblast lineage-specific overexpression of HECT domain E3 ubiquitin ligase Itch/Su(dx) or Nedd4 showed little inhibitory effect on the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutants.
source: Neuroblast lineage-specific overexpression of HECT domain E3 ubiquitin ligase Itch/Su(dx) or Nedd4, known for mediating Notch receptor polyubiquitination and degradation (Cornell et al., 1999; Le Bras et al., 2011; Qiu et al., 2000; Sakata et al., 2004; Wilkin et al., 2004), showed little inhibitory effect on the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutants (Figure 6A,B), suggesting that these two E3 ligases are not fully active upon overexpression in neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Simultaneous overexpression of Su(dx) and Ndfip led to a complete rescue of the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutants.
source: Whereas simultaneous overexpression of Nedd4 and Ndfip barely exhibited any effect on brain tumor phenotype caused by vps35 mutation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C), coexpression of Su(dx) and Ndfip indeed led to a complete rescue of the supernumerary neuroblast phenotype in vps35 mutants (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: The high accumulation of Notch in aberrant endosomal vesicles in vps35 mutant cells was effectively suppressed by Su(dx) and Ndfip coexpression.
source: Consistent with these observations, the high accumulation of Notch in aberrant endosomal vesicles in vps35 mutant cells was also effectively suppressed by Su(dx) and Ndfip coexpression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: Expression of either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-C917A by PntP1-Gal4 led to a mild neuroblast overproliferation phenotype.
source: Indeed, we observed a strong synergistic interaction between Su(dx) and Vps26 in mediating neuroblast self-renewal. While expression of either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-C917A, a dominant negative form of Su(dx) (Su(dx)-DN) that lacks its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (Wang et al., 2015), by PntP1-Gal4, led to a mild neuroblast overproliferation phenotype (Figure 6C,D), simultaneous expression of vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN resulted in a severe brain tumor phenotype (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Simultaneous expression of vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN resulted in a severe brain tumor phenotype.
source: Indeed, we observed a strong synergistic interaction between Su(dx) and Vps26 in mediating neuroblast self-renewal. While expression of either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-C917A, a dominant negative form of Su(dx) (Su(dx)-DN) that lacks its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (Wang et al., 2015), by PntP1-Gal4, led to a mild neuroblast overproliferation phenotype (Figure 6C,D), simultaneous expression of vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN resulted in a severe brain tumor phenotype (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Notch receptors were highly accumulated in enlarged Rab7-positive endosomal vesicles in neural progenitors expressing both vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN, but not in neural progenitors expressing either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-DN alone.
source: More significantly, Notch receptors were highly accumulated in enlarged Rab7-positive endosomal vesicles in neural progenitors expressing both vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN, but not in neural progenitors expressing either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-DN alone (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: Su(dx) mainly localized to the cell cortex, whereas Ndfip primarily distributed in intracellular vesicles.
source: Immunostaining with our newly-raised Su(dx) and Ndfip antibodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B) revealed that Su(dx) mainly localized to the cell cortex, whereas Ndfip primarily distributed in intracellular vesicles (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: The largely distinct distribution pattern of Su(dx) and Ndfip in INPs might partially explain why Notch polyubiquitination and lysosomal degradation is inherently inefficient in neural progenitors.
source: Such largely distinct distribution pattern of Su(dx) and Ndfip in INPs might partially explain why Notch polyubiquitination and lysosomal degradation is inherently inefficient in neural progenitors.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation of distinct subcellular localizations of Su(dx) and Ndfip.

claim: Blocking the entry to the ESCRT pathway via depletion of Hrs exhibited no effects on the brain tumor phenotypes in vps35 mutants.
source: A third prediction of this hypothesis is that ectopic processing and activation of the Notch receptor in vps35 mutants are independent of the ESCRT pathway. Indeed, blocking the entry to the ESCRT pathway via depletion of Hrs, a key subunit of ESCRT-0, exhibited no effects on the brain tumor phenotypes in vps35 mutants (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: Ectopic processing and activation of the Notch receptor in vps35 mutants are independent of the ESCRT pathway.
source: A third prediction of this hypothesis is that ectopic processing and activation of the Notch receptor in vps35 mutants are independent of the ESCRT pathway. Indeed, blocking the entry to the ESCRT pathway via depletion of Hrs, a key subunit of ESCRT-0, exhibited no effects on the brain tumor phenotypes in vps35 mutants (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: The claim is based on the observation that Hrs depletion does not suppress the vps35 mutant phenotype.

claim: Retromer prevents neural progenitor dedifferentiation through compensating the insufficient dampening of Notch signaling mediated by the Su(dx)/Ndfip-ESCRT-lysosomal pathway.
source: Taken together, these findings indicated that retromer prevents neural progenitor dedifferentiation through compensating the insufficient dampening of Notch signaling mediated by the Su(dx)/Ndfip-ESCRT-lysosomal pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on multiple lines of evidence including genetic interactions and rescue experiments.

claim: A smear of presumably ubiquitinated NICD migrating at approximately 130 kilodaltons (kDa) and a un-ubiquitinated NICD band migrating at 100 kDa specifically accumulated in vps35 mutant but not wild type brain extracts.
source: In accordance, our results clearly showed that, a smear of presumably ubiquitinated NICD migrating at approximately 130 kilodaltons (kDa) and a un-ubiquitinated NICD band migrating at 100 kDa specifically accumulated in vps35 mutant but not wild type brain extracts, indicating that these Notch fragments are hypo-ubiquitinated NICD (Figure 6I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The increased intensity of the smear of hypo-ubiquitinated Notch fragments in vps35 mutants was essentially reduced back to normal upon coexpression of Su(dx) and Ndfip.
source: Importantly, such increased intensity of the smear of these hypo-ubiquitinated Notch fragments in vps35 mutants (green arrowhead) was essentially reduced back to normal upon coexpression of Su(dx) and Ndfip (Figure 6I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Un-ubiquitinated NICD fragments specifically accumulated in larval brain extracts coexpressing vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN but not in extracts expressing either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-DN alone.
source: Consistently, un-ubiquitinated NICD fragments also specifically accumulated in larval brain extracts coexpressing vps26-RNAi and Su(dx)-DN but not in extracts expressing either vps26-RNAi or Su(dx)-DN alone (Figure 6J).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Accumulation of hypo-ubiquitinated NICD-GFP fragments was specifically detected in vps35 mutant but not wild type control brain extracts in N; NiGFP background.
source: Furthermore, in N; NiGFP background, in which a bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) transgene expressing a GFP-tagged Notch (NiGFP) functionally replaces endogenous Notch (Couturier et al., 2012), accumulation of hypo-ubiquitinated NICD-GFP fragments was also specifically detected in vps35 mutant but not wild type control brain extracts (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Blocking the cargo entry into the ESCRT pathway by Hrs downregulation potently inhibited the rescue effects of Su(dx)/Ndfip on retromer inactivation-induced brain tumor phenotype.
source: Indeed, blocking the cargo entry into the ESCRT pathway by Hrs downregulation potently inhibited the rescue effects of Su(dx)/Ndfip on retromer inactivation-induced brain tumor phenotype (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: Asymmetric partition of Numb leads to a biased internalization of the Notch receptor and hence asymmetric dampening of Notch signaling in neural progenitors.
source: Here we reveal that, while asymmetric partition of Numb leads to a biased internalization of the Notch receptor and hence asymmetric dampening of Notch signaling in neural progenitors, it meanwhile poses a high risk of non-canonical endosomal activation of Notch.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge and the findings of this study.

claim: Asymmetric partition of Numb poses a high risk of non-canonical endosomal activation of Notch.
source: Here we reveal that, while asymmetric partition of Numb leads to a biased internalization of the Notch receptor and hence asymmetric dampening of Notch signaling in neural progenitors, it meanwhile poses a high risk of non-canonical endosomal activation of Notch.
evidence: The claim is based on the findings of this study showing ectopic Notch activation in endosomes.

claim: The retromer complex is the key protein trafficking machinery that resolves the crisis of non-canonical endosomal activation of Notch through a timely retrieval of the Notch receptor from its endosomal activation compartments.
source: We find that the retromer complex is the key protein trafficking machinery that resolves this crisis through a timely retrieval of the Notch receptor from its endosomal activation compartments.
evidence: The claim is based on the combined findings of this study.

claim: Upon retromer dysfunction, neural progenitors dedifferentiate into neural stem cell-like status and result in the formation of transplantable tumors.
source: Upon retromer dysfunction, neural progenitors dedifferentiate into neural stem cell-like status and result in the formation of transplantable tumors.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data from MARCM analysis and transplantation assays.

claim: Retromer acts as a tumor suppressor in Drosophila larval brains.
source: Therefore, retromer acts as a tumor suppressor in Drosophila larval brains.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation that retromer dysfunction leads to tumor formation.

claim: Mammalian Vps35 physically interacts with Notch.
source: Importantly, mammalian Vps35 physically interacts with Notch, colocalizes with Notch in neural progenitors, and its neuroblast-lineage-specific expression fully rescues neural progenitor-derived brain tumor phenotype in vps35 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by coimmunoprecipitation experiments with mouse proteins.

claim: Mammalian Vps35 colocalizes with Notch in neural progenitors.
source: Importantly, mammalian Vps35 physically interacts with Notch, colocalizes with Notch in neural progenitors, and its neuroblast-lineage-specific expression fully rescues neural progenitor-derived brain tumor phenotype in vps35 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing colocalization of human Vps35 with Notch.

claim: Neuroblast-lineage-specific expression of mammalian Vps35 fully rescues neural progenitor-derived brain tumor phenotype in vps35 mutants.
source: Importantly, mammalian Vps35 physically interacts with Notch, colocalizes with Notch in neural progenitors, and its neuroblast-lineage-specific expression fully rescues neural progenitor-derived brain tumor phenotype in vps35 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic rescue experiments with human Vps35.

claim: The brain tumor suppressor function of retromer is likely to be conserved in mammals.
source: Thus, the brain tumor suppressor function of retromer is likely to be conserved in mammals.
evidence: The claim is based on the functional rescue with mammalian Vps35 and physical interaction with mammalian Notch.

claim: Downregulation of the retromer complex components has been reported in various human cancers, including glioblastoma.
source: Intriguingly, downregulation of the retromer complex components has been reported in various human cancers, including glioblastoma (An et al., 2012; Bredel et al., 2005; Lee et al., 2006b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: This study provides a new mechanistic link between the retromer complex and carcinogenesis.
source: Our studies thus provide a new mechanistic link between the retromer complex and carcinogenesis.
evidence: The claim is based on the findings of this study showing retromer's role in preventing tumor formation.

claim: Notch is probably not the only substrate of Su(dx) and Ndfip in neuroblasts or neural progenitors.
source: We speculate that Notch is probably not the only substrate of Su(dx) and Ndfip in neuroblasts or neural progenitors.
evidence: The claim is presented as speculation.

claim: High levels and/or activity of the Su(dx)/Ndfip E3 ubiquitin ligase system above certain threshold may potentially cause imbalanced homeostasis of its critical substrates and hence perturbed neuroblast lineages.
source: Therefore, high levels and/or activity of this E3 ubiquitin ligase system above certain threshold may potentially cause imbalanced homeostasis of its critical substrates and hence perturbed neuroblast lineages.
evidence: The claim is presented as speculation based on the observation that Su(dx)/Ndfip overexpression causes tissue atrophy.

claim: Co-overexpression of Su(dx) and Ndfip led to drastically reduced number of neuroblast lineages and severe tissue atrophy.
source: Indeed, co-overexpression of Su(dx) and Ndfip led to drastically reduced number of neuroblast lineages and severe tissue atrophy (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: A relatively general yet inefficient ubiquitination-degradation system coupled with a highly efficient and selective cargo retrieving system provides a customized regulation of the Notch receptor.
source: In this case, a relatively general yet inefficient ubiquitination-degradation system coupled with a highly efficient and selective cargo retrieving system provides a customized regulation of the Notch receptor, ensuring sufficient dampening of Notch signaling in neural progenitors without devastating side effects.
evidence: The claim is based on the combined findings and represents a model proposed by the authors.

claim: Retromer dysfunction causes increased levels of APP to reside in the endosomes for longer duration than normal, resulting in accelerated processing of APP into amyloid-β.
source: Intriguingly, previous studies posited that retromer dysfunction causes increased levels of APP (β-amyloid precursor protein) to reside in the endosomes for longer duration than normal, resulting in accelerated processing of APP into amyloid-β, a neurotoxic fragment implicated AD pathogenesis (Small and Gandy, 2006; Small and Petsko, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Retromer maintains the integrity of photoreceptors by avoiding persistent accumulation of rhodopsin in endolysosomal compartments that stresses photoreceptors and causes their degeneration.
source: Furthermore, retromer maintains the integrity of photoreceptors by avoiding persistent accumulation of rhodopsin in endolysosomal compartments that stresses photoreceptors and causes their degeneration (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Retromer serves as bomb squad to retrieve and disarm harmful or toxic protein fragments from endosomes in a timely manner and thereby safeguard the integrity and fitness of the neuronal lineages.
source: Taken together with our study here, these findings indicate that retromer serves as bomb squad to retrieve and disarm harmful or toxic protein fragments from endosomes in a timely manner and thereby safeguard the integrity and fitness of the neuronal lineages.
evidence: The claim is based on the combined findings from this study and previous studies.

claim: Notch is activated in MVBs in a ligand-dependent, cell-autonomous manner in vps35 mutants, distinct from the majority of non-canonical Notch activation mechanisms.
source: We favor the idea that Notch is activated in MVBs in a ligand-dependent, cell-autonomous manner, distinct from the majority of non-canonical Notch activation mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is presented as the authors' favored interpretation based on their experimental data.

claim: Most of the endosomal Notch activation events identified before are ligand-independent.
source: Most of the endosomal Notch activation events identified before, including ectopic Notch signaling activation in ESCRT mutants, BLOS2 mutants, or Rme8 and Vps26 double knockdown background, as well as Hif-alpha-dependent activation of Notch signaling implicated in crystal cell maintenance and survival, are all ligand-independent (Baron, 2012; Childress et al., 2006; Gallagher and Knoblich, 2006; Giebel and Wodarz, 2006; Gomez-Lamarca et al., 2015; Hori et al., 2011; Jaekel and Klein, 2006; Mukherjee et al., 2011; Palmer and Deng, 2015; Schneider et al., 2013; Thompson et al., 2005; Vaccari and Bilder, 2005; Vaccari et al., 2009; Wilkin et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Blocking the entry of Notch into the ESCRT pathway but not ligand inactivation potently inhibited ectopic Notch activation induced by ESCRT mutations.
source: Strongly supporting this notion, blocking the entry of Notch into the ESCRT pathway but not ligand inactivation potently inhibited ectopic Notch activation induced by ESCRT mutations (Childress et al., 2006; Gallagher and Knoblich, 2006; Jaekel and Klein, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Attenuating ligand activity but not preventing Notch from entering the ESCRT pathway effectively rescues Notch overactivation phenotype caused by retromer dysfunction.
source: In sharp contrast to these previously-revealed mechanisms, attenuating ligand activity but not preventing Notch from entering the ESCRT pathway effectively rescues Notch overactivation phenotype caused by retromer dysfunction (Figures 3D,E and 6G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3D,E and 6G,H.

claim: Upon retromer dysfunction, both Notch and Delta are entrapped in MVBs, where Notch and Delta are presented by limiting membrane and intravesicular membrane respectively and result in ligand-dependent Notch processing and activation.
source: We speculate that, upon retromer dysfunction, both Notch and Delta are entrapped in MVBs, where Notch and Delta are presented by limiting membrane and intravesicular membrane respectively and result in ligand-dependent Notch processing and activation, resembling the scenario presented for ligand-dependent Notch signaling activation in Sara endosome (Coumailleau et al., 2009; Kressmann et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is presented as speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: The ability of vps35 mutant neoplastic neuroblasts to metastasize upon transplantation is intriguing.
source: The ability of vps35 mutant neoplastic neuroblasts to metastasize upon transplantation is intriguing (Figure 1J,K).
evidence: The claim is based on the transplantation assay results.

claim: Metastasis of brain tumor cells derived from neuroblast lineages has never been observed in the developing fly larval brains.
source: Metastasis of brain tumor cells derived from neuroblast lineages has never been observed in the developing fly larval brains, likely because the limited time window of fly larval development precludes tumor progression and metastasis.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about fly development.

claim: Transplantation assay provides the ectopic microenvironment and allows cancer progression in a much longer time scale.
source: Transplantation assay (Rossi and Gonzalez, 2015), however, provides the ectopic microenvironment and allows cancer progression in a much longer time scale (months, or even years upon retransplantation).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about transplantation assays.

claim: Mutations that caused metastasis of fly brain tumor cells upon transplantation have also been implicated in various human cancers.
source: Importantly, mutations that caused metastasis of fly brain tumor cells upon transplantation have also been implicated in various human cancers (Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005; Eroglu et al., 2014; Froldi et al., 2015; Knoblich, 2010; Landskron et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2017; Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.
